content: Injected insulin regimens provide patients with the ability to adjust their dosing schedules, offering greater flexibility. However, these plans are associated with an increased risk of hypoglycemia. Multi-dose injection (MDI) therapy involves the administration of a long-acting basal insulin to maintain baseline glucose levels, combined with rapid-acting or ultra-rapid-acting insulin administered prior to meals to manage postprandial glucose spikes. NPH-based insulin regimens consist of injections that combine either regular insulin or short-acting insulin with NPH (Neutral Protamine Hagedorn) insulin. These regimens are typically suited for individuals who may benefit from a less intensive insulin therapy approach.
